data.review_target: codex-cli (gpt-5.5, "Beauvoir" explorer subagent) read-only subsystem readiness review of opentraces.ai dataset/workflow/publish/HF-remote/schema stack toward the 0.4 init->bucket->workflow->dataset->consume lifecycle

findings.claim_quote: High: the packaged CLI can accept an older schema package than the code now requires. `pyproject.toml` still allows `opentraces-schema>=0.3.0` while the installed schema package is `0.4.0` and 0.4.0 explicitly introduces the dataset/workflow contract. Current core code imports those 0.4 models directly, so a fresh install resolving `0.3.x` can fail before the lifecycle starts.
findings.why: Verified in captured output: pyproject has `opentraces-schema>=0.3.0,<1.0.0` (actually L13, review said L12 - off by one), version.py:3 is `SCHEMA_VERSION = "0.4.0"`, datasets.py:27 is `from opentraces_schema import (...)` pulling 0.4 dataset models. Logic is sound.

findings.claim_quote: High: `dataset publish` has a real-HF sync gap compared with the fake remote and legacy trace publisher. For real HF remotes, `_remote_row_ids` returns an empty set, `_check_remote_schema_not_ahead` no-ops, and changed-file detection treats every staged file as changed. The legacy `HFUploader` does fetch real remote `dataset_infos.json` and refuses newer schemas, but that path is separate.
findings.why: datasets.py:1042 `_check_remote_schema_not_ahead` confirmed: it early-returns when `_fake_remote_dir(repo_id) is None` (real HF -> no-op). `_remote_row_ids` def confirmed at L1098 but its body (returning empty set) was truncated from my extraction though it was inside the read sed range; same fake-remote idiom makes the empty-set claim highly plausible but not byte-confirmed here.

findings.claim_quote: High-risk consumption gap: the published dataset card points at `data/train.jsonl`, but dataset publish writes run-named shards. Local dataset creation creates `data/train.jsonl`, but `_stage_publication` writes `data/{contributor}-{run_id}-{digest}.jsonl`. The real HF loader behavior is unverifiable from code alone, but the repo evidence shows a config/path mismatch that can affect `datasets.load_dataset` for eval/model consumers.
findings.why: datasets.py:195 confirmed writes `data/train.jsonl`; datasets.py:1015-1018 confirmed shard name `f"{_safe_slug(contributor)}-{run_id}-{digest.hexdigest()[:12]}.jsonl"`. The card-points-at-train.jsonl leg (cited L1448) was not in my extracted slice, so the third anchor is unconfirmed, but review honestly hedged the load_dataset impact as 'unverifiable from code alone'.

findings.claim_quote: Medium-high: workflow execution is still a local harness, not a remote/job-ready runner. `current-agent` writes instructions and returns success without executing work; `claude-code-headless` either uses fake test rows or raises that real invocation is disabled. `--resume` is reserved, run records hardcode `candidate_count=0`, and the dataset lock is a non-atomic local `.lock` file.
findings.why: All four sub-claims confirmed in read source: L89 current-agent writes empty output + emitted_count=0; L176 _execute_claude_code_headless uses FAKE env rows or raises ExecutorUnavailableError; dataset.py:676-678 '--resume is reserved' + sys.exit(10); L316 class _dataset_lock is a plain file existence/write (non-atomic); candidate_count=0 hardcoded confirmed in _run_record builder.

findings.claim_quote: Medium: local-vs-remote abstractions overlap and some docs are stale. `dataset remote` delegates to root HF helper functions, the legacy root `remote` group still exists, top-level `push` still publishes `TraceRecord` shards, and top-level `pull` imports HF traces into the local inbox rather than syncing datasets. `remote_index.py` says dataset publish refreshes the cache, but the save path is in legacy `cli/publish.py`, not `core/datasets.py`.
findings.why: Strong: __init__.py:2984 confirmed legacy `remote` group with docstring 'Legacy project remote commands; use `ot dataset remote`'; remote_index.py:12-14 docstring claims 'dataset publish refreshes it' while the actual fetch/cache-save is in publish.py:585-590 legacy push path - a genuinely sharp catch. dataset.py:74 anchors the delegation slightly imprecisely (points at DatasetRemoteSummary dataclass; the real root_cli delegation is L87-89 in the same read region).

findings.claim_quote: Medium: dataset row validation/features are too shallow for robust ML consumption. Dataset rows get only simple top-level JSON-schema checks, and local HF feature generation maps arrays/objects to coarse fallbacks. That is adequate for the current minimal local dataset loop, but not yet strong enough for typed ml-intern/eval/model consumers.
findings.why: datasets.py:1376 validate_row confirmed: only top-level required-field + type=='object' checks, no deep typing. schema.py:65 _feature_for_annotation confirmed to fall back to coarse _JSON for arrays/open-ended shapes. datasets.py:1479 feature-gen leg not in my extracted slice but consistent with read schema.py evidence.

findings.claim_quote: How It Works Today ... `init` enrolls a project ... There is no first-class `bucket` object in the reviewed code. The closest current primitives are `DatasetCandidateQuery`, `CandidatePacket`, trace maps, and the run packet's query/scope fields. ... Workflows are local skill packages under `.opentraces/workflows` ... Datasets are local HF-shaped directories under `.opentraces/datasets`. ... Publish stages a public surface, filters blocked/review rows, uploads via `HfApi.upload_folder`, then marks rows uploaded and appends a local publication event. Legacy `push` is separate.
findings.why: Descriptive 'how it works' synthesis over files the review demonstrably read (all listed paths appear in the 63 tool-call command set: datasets.py, workflow_runner.py, workflows.py, upload.py, cli/__init__.py, schema dataset.py/trace_index.py). The 'no first-class bucket object' observation matches repo state at base_commit. Many line anchors not individually re-verified, but no contradiction found and the corpus was opened in full.

findings.claim_quote: Readiness Gaps ... For remote jobs, schedules are local-file triggers and run execution is not a real queue/worker contract. The schema has `DatasetRunRecord`, but not remote job IDs, leases, retry state, artifact URIs, worker identity, or input revision anchors.
findings.why: schedules.py read confirms local-file trigger backend ('backend':'local-file', schedule.trigger path) at L170-177; schema dataset.py was read and DatasetRunRecord exists. The 'no job IDs/leases/retry/artifact URIs' negative claim is consistent with the read schema (no such fields observed in the dumped dataset.py model region).

findings.claim_quote: For ml-intern/eval/model consumption, the project has a promising HF-shaped local dataset surface, but needs a stricter public row contract, stable split/config semantics, real remote schema/index inspection, withdrawal-aware consumption guidance, and probably explicit eval/model metadata rather than relying on arbitrary workflow rows.
findings.why: Forward-looking recommendation synthesizing f2/f3/f6 (real-remote inspection gap, path mismatch, shallow validation). No new file citation; it is an opinion/roadmap statement, appropriately uncited and consistent with the grounded defects above.

findings.claim_quote: For remote session sync, the strongest existing pieces are `TraceRecord.session_id`, `generation_index`, `git_links`, and the legacy remote index. Dataset publish does not yet use that index or expose a bidirectional session sync protocol.
findings.why: Mixed positive/gap statement. The legacy RemoteIndex (content_hashes, session_generations) was read in remote_index.py and the gap that dataset publish does not consume it aligns with f2/f5. session_id/generation_index/git_links are real TraceRecord fields visible in models.py the review read. No file:line given but it is an accurate orientation note.

findings.claim_quote: Read-only review only. I used memory to orient to the Plan 56/57/58 intent, but all current claims below are grounded in the checked-out repo. No files were edited; I did not run pytest.
findings.why: Method/scope disclosure. Consistent with the trace: all 63 tool calls are read-only (rg/sed/nl/wc/git status/--help); no Edit/Write tool calls and no pytest invocation present. The memory-orientation caveat matches the oai-mem citations appended to the message.

data.review_target: A codex-cli (gpt-5.5) code review of the opentraces 0.4 branch, emitting a structured codex-review envelope (3 findings + overall verdict) on the new branch-workflow / PR-blame consumer and remote-bucket resource path at base commit b2d504c.

findings.claim_quote: [P2] Quote traced intent before rendering PR Markdown
findings.why: Title of finding 1; framed as a P2 trust-boundary defect in PR-body rendering of captured user intent.

findings.claim_quote: When a captured user intent contains Markdown/HTML or PR-control text, `_pick_headline_intent` has only run secret redaction and sentinel stripping, and this appends it raw to the generated PR body. That lets trace content add headings, mentions, links, or break the later sections in auto-created PRs; the same intent is also rendered in commit details. Render it as escaped or quoted text before inserting it into Markdown.
findings.why: At the reviewed base commit b2d504c, _pick_headline_intent routes through redact_intent which ALREADY demotes leading '#' headings (_LEADING_HEADING_RE, line 281), collapses fence breakouts (_FENCE_BREAKOUT_RE, line 280) and strips sentinels, then wraps the result in _quote_intent (blockquote). So 'appends it raw' and the heading/section-break sub-claims are false; only @mentions and [links] are genuinely un-neutralized. The recommended fix (quote it) is already implemented.

findings.claim_quote: [P2] Include workflow digest in branch-run cache hits
findings.why: Title of finding 2; P2 correctness bug in branch-run caching.

findings.claim_quote: Cache hits are keyed only by the branch scope digest, so if the installed workflow package changes while base/head commits stay the same, this returns previously generated rows and never runs the new script/schema unless the caller knows to pass `force=True`. Since `execute_workflow` already records `workflow_digest`, include that digest in the cache key or validate cached metadata before returning a hit.
findings.why: Verified: run_branch_workflow's cache key is branch_run_output_path(scope_digest, llm_polish suffix) only (no workflow_digest); the hit at line 223 returns cached rows unless force=True. execute_workflow does record workflow_digest (workflow_runner.py:152/204/221/533). Claim matches code precisely.

findings.claim_quote: [P2] Replay TrailEvents for remote ot resources
findings.why: Title of finding 3; P2 correctness bug on the remote-bucket ot:// resolution path.

findings.claim_quote: With `trace get ot://... --remote-bucket` on a fresh checkout, this path pulls trace records and rebuilds the Trace Index but never replays the bucket TrailEvents before the later `resolve_resource(Path.cwd(), ref)` call. The resource resolver reads the repo event log, so remote-only Trail resources still resolve as unknown even though the bucket contains the export; use the trail replay helper for `ot://` refs or reject that combination.
findings.why: Verified: trace_get --remote-bucket calls pull_remote_bucket_for_trace (only remote_pull + rebuild_index, NO replay; _remote_bucket.py:9-36), then the ot:// branch calls resolve_resource(Path.cwd(), ref) reading the local repo event log. A replay helper (pull_remote_bucket_for_trail / restore_trail_events_to_repo, _remote_bucket.py:39-56) exists but is not used on this path. Cited line 875-877 drifted to ~935-940 in the base-commit file but the symbol and behavior are exactly as described.

findings.claim_quote: overall_correctness: patch is incorrect
findings.why: The review's verdict field. Resting on f1/f2/f3; f2 and f3 are grounded so a 'needs changes' verdict is defensible, but f1 (its trust-boundary headline) is a misread, weakening the strength of the verdict.

findings.claim_quote: The patch introduces correctness issues in the new branch workflow cache and remote-bucket resource path, plus a PR-body trust-boundary bug for traced intent. These should be addressed before considering the changes correct.
findings.why: overall_explanation. Two of three named issues (branch workflow cache, remote-bucket resource path) are grounded; the third (PR-body trust-boundary) is overstated because heading/section-break injection is already neutralized at the reviewed commit.

data.review_target: A codex-cli (gpt-5.5, xhigh) full-project review of the opentraces.ai repo on the 0.4 branch (team-of-agents, read-only), reporting findings on staleness/simplification ahead of the init=>bucket=>workflow=>dataset=>consume change. Primary findings deliverable is step 38; additional concrete conclusions in steps 922 and 1460.

findings.claim_quote: Packaging is not safe for 0.4 yet. `pyproject.toml` still allows `opentraces-schema>=0.3.0`, while this branch imports 0.4 dataset symbols directly. A fresh install can resolve an older schema and fail at import time.
findings.why: Review's own observations confirm version.py read as SCHEMA_VERSION="0.4.0" (step 23) and pyproject pin >=0.3.0 (step 25); datasets.py imports 0.4 dataset symbols. Pin is genuinely looser than the imported symbols' floor. Line cited 12 vs actual 13 is a minor off-by-one but the claim holds.

findings.claim_quote: `dataset publish` is not yet as robust as the old HF trace publisher. Real HF remote row/schema inspection is mostly stubbed or shallow, while the old `HFUploader` has real remote `dataset_infos.json` schema-ahead refusal. Also, dataset creation/card metadata points at `data/train.jsonl`, but publish writes run-named shards, which is risky for `datasets.load_dataset` and downstream eval/model consumption.
findings.why: Review observations confirm datasets.py card writes data_file="data/train.jsonl" (step 11 obs line 405) and HFUploader exposes DatasetRemoteSchemaAheadError (step 9 obs); review explicitly reasoned about the card-vs-run-named-shards mismatch (step 27 obs). The card/shards mismatch is a concrete, verifiable claim.

findings.claim_quote: Workflows are still a local scaffold, not a remote job system. `current-agent` returns instructions rather than executing; `claude-code-headless` is disabled except fake test rows; `dataset run --resume` is reserved. That is fine for current local UAT, but not enough for remote jobs.
findings.why: Review's observation of workflow_runner.py shows status="instructions" (line 114) for the current-agent path and the executor allow-set {current-agent, claude-code-headless} (step 22 obs), directly supporting the 'returns instructions rather than executing' claim.

findings.claim_quote: Latest branch behavior has integration drift. Adaptive burst gap exists in core, but CLI passes fixed `DEFAULT_BURST_GAP`; survival-cache writes exist, but normal `trail track --patch` does not read them back.
findings.why: Live code confirms bursts.py has an adaptive-gap layer (Cluster H, gap=None requests adaptive) yet CLI trace.py does `gap = burst_gap if burst_gap is not None else DEFAULT_BURST_GAP`, substituting the fixed default instead of passing None, which defeats adaptive selection. sync.py has survival-cache build/append functions matching the 'writes exist' claim. The trail-track-not-reading-back half is plausible but I did not fully trace the read path; line numbers have drifted from the reviewed commit.

findings.claim_quote: The public surface is cleaner than the repo around it. ... But docs, `skill/SKILL.md`, `introspect`, web/TUI clients, and hidden commands still describe `push/pull/remote/web/tui/list/add` and older Trail verbs.
findings.why: introspect exists at __init__.py:4235 (step 17 obs) as a machine-discovery surface, and the flat-roots-dropped logic is real. The claim that docs/skill still describe old verbs was true at the reviewed commit; note the CURRENT working tree skill/SKILL.md was since edited to explicitly exclude push/pull/web/tui from the public tree, so this specific staleness has partly been fixed post-review (groundedness assessed against review-time state).

findings.claim_quote: The clean 0.4 shape should be: `init` enrolls the repo and capture sources. `bucket` stores a named query/candidate set from Trace Map/Trace Index. `workflow` is the recipe/job contract that transforms buckets into rows. `dataset` is curation, review, materialization, remotes, publish. `consume` is typed downstream use: HF load, evals, and ml-intern model/eval recipes.
findings.why: This is the review's design recommendation/verdict synthesizing the lifecycle the user asked about; it is grounded in the read CLI grouping and matches the user's stated init=>bucket=>workflow=>dataset=>consume goal. Recommendation rather than a defect claim.

findings.claim_quote: I would remove or de-emphasize these now: legacy root command implementations that are imported then dropped, ... the old `.agent-trace/traces.jsonl` hook side-channel, old `ot://trace/<id>/patches/...` alias after fixtures migrate, hard-coded burst path prefix, and unused `_anchor_with_survival`. The web/TUI inbox review loop is also stale because it shells out to removed `opentraces push`.
findings.why: server.py:720 (at the review's base commit b2d504cd, an ancestor of HEAD) is inside the api_push endpoint that FAILS CLOSED, returning a 410 with a 'Legacy trace push is disabled in the v0.4 flow' message, NOT a shell-out to `opentraces push`. The review cited a real file:line but mischaracterized the disabled/fail-closed handler as a live shell-out to a removed command. The broader 'unused _anchor_with_survival / hard-coded burst prefix' sub-claims were not verified and may be grounded; the web-shell-out sub-claim is the misread.

findings.claim_quote: The current branch has the beginnings of the right model, but only projections are actually bucket-shaped today. Local bucket exists only as path helpers ... TraceRecords are still written to `~/.opentraces/projects/<slug>/traces/<trace-id>.jsonl` during ingest ... `trace index rebuild` reads from project trace stores and staging, not bucket origin.
findings.why: Multi-citation structural finding consistent with step 38's 'no first-class bucket yet'; ingest writing to project traces (ingest.py:379) and trace_index reading project/staging are corroborated by the review's reads in steps 21-22 and 12. Line numbers cited against the reviewed commit; structural claim is sound.

findings.claim_quote: I inspected it. The dataset is useful as a raw evidence archive, but not yet as a clean eval dataset. ... Rows 52 ... Publication state 51 blocked, 1 needs review. Main issue: the rows embed full trajectories, including raw prompts/tool output/path/hash-heavy content. That is why the security gate blocks almost everything.
findings.why: Empirical inspection of a live local dataset with concrete row/size/publication-state metrics; the review actually ran the inspection (per its narration). The quantitative claims (52 rows, 51 blocked) are checkable artifacts though I did not re-run the inspection; the qualitative conclusion (security gate blocks due to embedded full trajectories) follows from the stated metrics.

findings.claim_quote: `command.args` is polluted in 8 historical rows with injected skill body text. ... 6 of those have a mismatch between labelled skill and injected body skill, e.g. label `browse` but body says `deep-research`. ... Outcomes are session-level, not command-level. In multi-command traces this can leak or mislabel command success.
findings.why: Precise quantitative dataset-quality claims (8 polluted rows, 6 with label/body mismatch, specific browse-vs-deep-research example) presented as inspection output. Plausible and specific enough to be real, but I could not re-run the row-level inspection to confirm the exact counts; flagging as a candidate for deterministic re-check against the dataset rows.

findings.claim_quote: The evidence layer is coherent: canonical Trace Trails live in the local Git ref `refs/opentraces/local/events/v1`, with derived SQLite/FTS trace index and workflow-neutral Trace Map projections. TrailEvents are local replay evidence, not publishable schema rows.
findings.why: Positive characterization of the evidence layer; the canonical ref name refs/opentraces/local/events/v1 and the trace-index/trace-map projection split match the project's own documented architecture and the review's reads (steps 12, 20).

findings.claim_quote: I did not edit files or run the full pytest suite; this was a read-only branch/code/docs review with five focused agents plus local live-help and branch inspection.
findings.why: Scope/limitation disclosure. Corroborated by the trace: normalized_tool_calls show five spawn_agent calls and live `.venv/bin/opentraces --help`/branch git inspection, with no apply_patch edits in the review portion and no full pytest run observed.

Since `execute_workflow` already records `workflow_digest`, include that digest in the cache key or validate cached metadata before returning a hit.
